title: The Smell Postcards
clue: Little dishes of faraway places, set at nose height for an old friend.
reveal: Collect small, safe scents from places your senior dog has loved. Your dog votes for a postcard with their nose, and the winning place becomes their next outing, or just a story and a snack at home.
objective: Set out tiny scent souvenirs from your dog's favorite places, see which one holds their attention longest, and let that place star next.
instructions: Think of three or four places your dog has loved: a trail, the beach, a park, a grandparent's yard. You need only a blade of grass, a clean twig or a pinch of sand from each.
Check each one is clean and too large to swallow in one gulp. Skip anything prickly, moldy or treated. Keep souvenirs to grass, a clean twig and a pinch of sand.
Place each souvenir on its own saucer or paper plate on a low mat, close to where your dog rests. Label each with the place name.
Bring your dog over gently, only if they want to come. Do not lead them to any plate.
Watch which postcard holds their nose longest, and which one makes the tail move. Take your time. Note the winner.
Sit near the winning postcard and tell the story of the place quietly, with a treat from the day's food.
If the place is easy to reach, plan a gentle outing there in good weather. If not, the souvenirs go back in a jar for another day.
twist: Your dog picks a destination with their nose, and the winning smell decides the next little outing.
variations: Yard version: collect a blade of grass from your own garden each season.
Seated version: bring the plates to your dog's bed so they can stay lying down.
Two-postcard version: only two choices, closer together.
Keepsake version: write the winning place on the postcard.
completion: It counts once your dog has sniffed at least one postcard and you have shared its place story. Stop if they walk away.
photoIdea: Your dog sniffing the winning postcard, close and low, with natural light on the gray muzzle.
memoryPrompt: Which place won the sniff, and what do you remember about going there?
substitutes: No souvenirs? Use a blade of grass or a dry leaf from your own safe garden.
dietNotes: A single small treat from the day's food. Ask your vet about your senior dog's diet.
safety: Use only grass, a clean twig or a pinch of sand, too large to swallow. Take them away if your dog mouths them.
Set the plates at your dog's resting height so they never need to stand up, stretch or climb.
Let your dog walk away at any time, and follow your vet's advice on activity.
